resolution_of_cited_issue_3582.citation: mermaid-js/mermaid#3582, open since 2022-10-05, still open and last touched 2025-03-19
resolution_of_cited_issue_3582.rationale: This issue is genuinely on-topic and unresolved: it asks how to notate an attribute that is simultaneously part of a composite primary key and a foreign key — exactly the TASK_VERSION-adjacent shape the brief's acid list needs for OUTCOME_RULE, NAMED_RESOURCE_LINK, and CONDITION_POST. It corroborates, from the issue tracker rather than the grammar alone, the sibling source-mermaid-erd-grammar.json record's classification: the grammar accepts `PK, FK` as a comma-separated key-token list on one row, but there is no dedicated composite-key grouping construct, and nearly four years on, no maintainer has closed this gap or even proposed a syntax. Marking two attribute rows both PK, as the grammar allows, produces two independent single-column key flags, not a composite-key semantic — the open issue is direct evidence that real authors hit exactly this ambiguity and get no answer from the project.

resolution_of_cited_issue_442.rationale: This issue has no bearing on erDiagram or any advanced construct in this survey. It is a 2016 announcement of a third-party VSCode preview extension, filed and closed years before Mermaid's ER diagram type existed as a documented feature. Recorded here explicitly, as instructed, to correct the sibling records' citation: whatever those records intended #442 to support, this record finds no relevant content in it, and it should not be relied on for any claim about erDiagram. This is reported as a factual finding about the issue's content, not as an accusation about how the citation arose.

enumerated_string_domain_workaround_only.citation: mermaid-js/mermaid#3400, closed 2024-08-18 without a native feature
enumerated_string_domain_workaround_only.rationale: The issue asks the same question FOLDER_RUN.execution_context and NAMED_RESOURCE_LINK.link_kind need answered — how to constrain a column to a fixed value set — and was closed roughly two years after being opened with no native `enum(...)` type ever added to the grammar (independently confirmed: the sibling source-mermaid-erd-grammar.json record's ATTRIBUTE_KEY/type-token analysis shows no enum production). The two workarounds the community settled on in the thread — a free-text comment string listing the values, or a synthetic side-table named with an `Enum` suffix and no way to visually mark it as an enumeration type — are both outside the language's own semantics and unverifiable by any parser or validator. A comment thread from 2026-01-26, well after closure, shows the underlying need is still unmet.

unique_key_reported_broken_not_merely_ab.rationale: This goes beyond the multi-column-UNIQUE gap the brief's acid list names for PLAN(domain_id, odate) and NAMED_RESOURCE(domain_id, name): it reports that even a single-column UK marker, which sibling records document as grammar-accepted, breaks diagram rendering in practice for the reporter. No multi-column UNIQUE construct exists at all in the grammar (the same absence of any attribute-grouping production that blocks composite primary keys — see source-mermaid-erd-grammar.json), so the multi-column case is necessarily not-expressible; this issue adds that even the simpler single-column case has a live, still-open rendering defect on top of that absence.

nullable_marker_added_but_purely_cosmeti.citation: erTypes.ts Attribute interface (`keys: ('PK' | 'FK' | 'UK')[]`, no 'NN' or nullable field) and merged PR #7793 ('feat(er): support optional attribute types', shipped in 11.16.0, present in 11.16.1); open issue #4429 requesting a first-class `NN` key
nullable_marker_added_but_purely_cosmeti.rationale: A `?` suffix on the attribute type (`string? alias`) was added and has shipped in the exact version (11.16.1) these records examine, and it postdates every sibling Mermaid record's stated retrieval date of 2026-08-14, so it is easy to mistake for a solved nullable-FK story. Reading erTypes.ts directly at the 11.16.1 tag shows the suffix is not: the PR's own description says it is 'preserving the literal `?` in the rendered type text', and the Attribute interface's `type` field remains a bare `string` with no separate boolean or enum nullable field — the `?` is indistinguishable, in the parsed model, from a user typing any other character into the free-text type column. It cannot be asserted, queried, or validated as a semantic nullable flag; it is decoration. Issue #4429, requesting a proper `NN` attribute key parallel to `PK`/`FK`/`UK`, remains open (last updated 2025-07-10) precisely because this cosmetic suffix does not satisfy the request. TASK_INSTANCE.folder_run_id and TASK_INSTANCE.plan_id's nullable-FK requirement is therefore still expressible-only-via-workaround (a documentation-only annotation with no enforcement), not expressible, despite the new syntax.

no_semantic_validation_undeclared_entity.citation: erDb.ts addEntity() (lines 54-74) and addRelationship() (lines 113-129); erDiagram.jison relationship productions (lines ~124-180), all at mermaid@11.16.1; corroborated by open issue #8054 (2026-08-12), reproduced explicitly on mermaid@11.16.1
no_semantic_validation_undeclared_entity.rationale: Direct reading of the pinned-tag grammar shows every one of the five relationship-statement productions calls `yy.addEntity()` unconditionally on both operands before calling `yy.addRelationship()`. addEntity() has no failure mode — if the name is not already in the entities map, it creates a bare, attribute-less entity node on the spot and logs an info-level message, nothing more. There is no code path anywhere in erDb.ts that rejects a relationship naming an entity that was never given its own attribute block: such an entity is silently manufactured as an empty box the instant it is first mentioned in a relationship line. A typo in an entity name (e.g. referencing TASK_VERSON instead of TASK_VERSION in one relationship among 30) produces no error, no warning, and no non-zero exit from mermaid-cli — it produces a 26th, empty phantom entity and a relationship pointing at it, with the diagram still parsing 'successfully'. Issue #8054, opened two days before this search and reproduced identically on 11.6.0 and the current-latest 11.16.1, demonstrates the same underlying absence of model-level integrity checking through a different trigger (an unescaped quote silently splitting one declared entity into several phantom fragments) — the issue's own words, 'the diagram parses cleanly and renders a different graph from the one they wrote', describe exactly the risk profile this code reading predicts for the acid-test question of whether a relationship referencing an undeclared entity is silently accepted. It is: not merely accepted, but invisibly promoted to a real entity with no way for a reader or a CI gate to distinguish a genuine 26th entity from a typo.

grouping_construct_merged_but_not_yet_re.citation: PR #7792 (merged to develop 2026-06-11, resolving feature request #7417); GitHub Compare API showing the merge commit is not an ancestor of either the mermaid@11.16.0 or mermaid@11.16.1 tag (status: diverged, behind_by 75 and 90 respectively); zero matches for 'subgraph' or 'namespace' in the pinned-tag erDiagram.jison; open issue #3225 (2022-07-15, 14 comments, still open) requesting the same capability
grouping_construct_merged_but_not_yet_re.rationale: Two distinct findings, both contrary to treating the several-logical-schemas gap as closed or closing. First, timing: #7792 adds a `subgraph`/`end` grouping block to erDiagram and was merged before both the 11.16.0 (2026-06-25) and 11.16.1 (2026-08-04) release dates, which could suggest it shipped in the exact version these records examine — but the Compare API shows the merge commit is not an ancestor of either release tag, and a direct grep of the grammar file at the 11.16.1 tag confirms zero occurrences of the token, so the feature has not actually reached any tagged release as of this search; a naive date-only inference would have wrongly concluded it had. Second, even once released, the PR's own description characterises it as a rendering/clustering aid ('grouping entities into logical domains', 'improves diagram clarity') built on the same entity namespace as ordinary entities — nothing in the PR text describes namespace-scoped identifiers, cross-schema uniqueness enforcement, or any validation tied to schema boundaries, which is what 'several logical schemas inside one database' requires per research question 10 (matching ADR-0001's configuration/runtime/audit/resources split). It is the same visual-grouping category as a flowchart subgraph, not a schema construct. Issue #3225's persistence for over four years across 14 comments, entirely unaddressed by #7792 per its own resolves-link (#7417, not #3225), is separate evidence that the specific 'group by category, still readable' need remains open even discounting the release-timing question.

layout_and_legibility_degrade_well_below.citation: mermaid-js/mermaid#4754 (open, 2023-08-21), #5409 (open, 2024-03-24, ~8 entities/~15 relationships), #3585 (open, 2022-10-05, AdventureWorks-scale schema), #6047 (open, 2024-11-10, 6 entities/5 relationships freezes the renderer)
layout_and_legibility_degrade_well_below.rationale: All four issues are open and describe entity-box overlap, arrow-edge collision, excessive diagram width breaking zoom, and outright renderer freezes. Critically, #6047's reproduction case that freezes the UI has only 6 entities and 5 relationships, and #5409's overlap case has roughly 8 entities and 15 relationships — both far below Gigacron's 25 entities and ~30 relationships. None of these issues were closed as fixed at time of search. This is direct evidence that the legibility and stability problems the brief's completion_criteria implicitly worry about (25 entities in a single diagram being unreadable) are not merely a hypothetical concern at Gigacron's scale — they are reported, open, unresolved defects at scales smaller than Gigacron's model, with no per-issue indication of a fix landing before mermaid@11.16.1.

validator_exit_behaviour_is_blunt_and_po.citation: mermaid-js/mermaid-cli#245 (closed 2022-06-27, unclear error message with no offending-line indication) and #903 (closed 2025-06-11, confirms mermaid-cli halts the entire batch and produces no output for any block, correct or not, on a single syntax error, with no way to isolate which of several diagrams failed)
validator_exit_behaviour_is_blunt_and_po.rationale: This does not contradict the sibling source-mermaid-erd-tooling.json record's likely finding that mermaid-cli exits non-zero on a malformed diagram (a genuinely usable CI-gate property, not disputed here); it adds a documented-limitations layer on top of that binary pass/fail signal. #903's own description of current behaviour — 'the entire conversion process halts... An error message... is displayed, and the process exits' — is itself confirmation of fail-fast exit behaviour, but the feature request exists precisely because that failure is all-or-nothing with no per-diagram isolation, and #245 documents that the resulting error message does not identify which line is at fault. For a 25-entity, ~30-relationship single-file model, this means a single typo anywhere produces a hard failure with a message that (per #245, admittedly from 2022) may not localise the fault, which is a materially weaker CI-gate diagnostic experience than the exit-code contract alone would suggest.

contrary_evidence_search.result: Both issue numbers named in the task were resolved: #3582 is genuinely on-topic (composite PK/FK notation, open and unresolved since 2022) and corroborates the grammar-level composite-key gap; #442 is unrelated to erDiagram entirely (a 2016 VSCode-extension announcement, closed 2017) and should not be relied on as evidence for any claim in the sibling records that cite it. Substantive, on-topic contrary evidence was found for six of the ten acid-list constructs (composite key: #3582; enumerated domain: #3400; multi-column/single-column unique: #2933; nullable FK: #4429 plus the erTypes.ts/PR-7793 cosmetic-suffix finding; several logical schemas: #3225 plus the PR-7792 timing/scope finding; and, outside the ten-construct list but explicitly named in the task, absence of semantic validation on undeclared entities: erDb.ts/erDiagram.jison code reading plus issue #8054) and for the layout/legibility-at-scale and validator-diagnosability angles (four and two issues respectively).
